extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. VoiceAssistant-Eval comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual and auditory inputs were extracted from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. To evaluate voice personalization, texts from RoleBench were utilized. Speech instructions were synthesized using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models to replace original text instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data was collected from 47 datasets in total: 23 audio understanding datasets (10 for Speech, 6 for Sound, 4 for Music, 3 for General), 11 text datasets, 11 audio datasets, and MMMU for the Viewing subset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Texts were preprocessed to ensure high synthesis quality: 1. Image references: Special tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases. 2. Text rewriting: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct was used to rewrite text to be more suitable for TTS. 3. Multiple-Choice Questions: Options were rephrased for better readability. Speech was synthesized using F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, evaluated with UTMOS Strong, and transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 to select the sample with the lowest word error rate.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, with manual review. (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances (e.g., corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, incorrect answers). (3) Categorization into 13 predefined task categories. (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Curators reviewed each item on a single screen and assigned a Good or Bad verdict. Manual review proceeded in three passes: (1) Media integrity: Verifying audio and images are present, decodable, audible, and visible. (2) Task well-posedness: Confirming the prompt is clear and inputs align with the task. (3) Answer validity: Checking that reference answers are consistent with the prompt and media, and multi-turn items are coherent.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, UTMOS Strong, Whisper-Large-v3
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The creators will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Voice/speaker timbre and role-play voice imitation. The dataset also includes safety tasks that may contain potentially dangerous, unethical, biased, or harmful user queries, as well as requests for personal information (e.g., addresses).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to help researchers better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies. It includes safety cards and anti-impersonation safeguards to enable research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited linguistic diversity (monolingual focus on English, with only five Chinese roles). Relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise and bias. Gaps in task coverage and scenario realism (e.g., lacks video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming). Evaluates models in an offline, static manner, failing to capture real-world deployment factors like latency, continuous listening, and barge-in.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluating and benchmarking the listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities of AI assistants. Not supposed to be used for training models for cheating.
